sub_question: SQ0: Which air-quality parameters should the monitor measure, and what are the health-relevant thresholds?
summary: An air-quality monitor should measure the six WHO 'classical' pollutants (PM2.5, PM10, O3, NO2, SO2, CO) plus environmental co-parameters (temperature, humidity, pressure) and, for indoor use, CO2 and TVOCs. WHO 2021 AQG limits give the respiratory-relevant thresholds.
key_insight: The scientifically-grounded minimum sensor set = 6 WHO classical pollutants. PM2.5 is the single most health-critical (penetrates lungs+bloodstream, drives COPD/asthma/stroke). WHO 2021 AQG limits (much stricter than 2005) give ready-made thresholds to power respiratory alerts.

PM2.5.note: fine particles, penetrate lungs+bloodstream; most health-critical

notes: Numeric AQG values are the published WHO 2021 Global Air Quality Guidelines figures; pollutant list corroborated across 3 WHO pages + NIH mirror. Averaging-period structure (annual/peak = long-term; 24h/8h = short-term) confirmed on the feature-story page.
